reviews.summary: After weeks of riding it in Brazil, the Brazilian Brothers say the 2026 Nitro fixes the earlier versions' inconsistent lift, with softer landings from big jumps and loops. It stays one of the easiest kites to learn kiteloops on, with light bar pressure and little yank, but it needs 25+ knots and overpowered riding and is not a strapless or foil kite.

structured_review.summary: An easy, intuitive 5-strut big air kite and one of the friendliest kites for learning kiteloops: light bar pressure, little yank and a fast loop. The 2026 version fixes the inconsistent lift of earlier Nitros, but it only really comes alive overpowered in 25+ knots and is not meant for strapless or foil.
pros: Among the easiest kites to learn kiteloops on: fast loop with little yank
More consistent lift and softer landings than previous Nitros
Very light bar pressure, especially in the A setting
Big sweet spot for jumping; accessible to intermediate riders
cons: Needs strong wind (25+ knots) for its best jumps
Not suited to strapless or foil riding
Less user-friendly than the Switchblade for general riding
structured_review.best_for: Intermediate to advanced twin-tip riders learning and progressing kiteloops in strong wind.
structured_review.not_for: Light-wind riders, or anyone wanting one kite for foil and strapless.
structured_review.rec_blurb: Loop school in a kite: light, fast, and very little yank.
